front: Power Apps / Power Automate / Dataverse in one line
back: Apps: build applications low-code. Automate: automate processes. Dataverse: the shared, secured data backbone they all build on.
Hundreds of prebuilt bridges to Microsoft and third-party services — the triggers and actions apps and flows use, no custom integration code.
Secure, data-driven external websites on the Dataverse foundation — customers and partners interacting with business data.
Where organisations build agents: conversational AI grounded in company knowledge, able to take actions, published to channels.
The analytics member of the family: connects to data, models it, and presents it as interactive reports and dashboards that the other Power Platform pieces can link to.
Building applications mainly through configuration and visual designers, with code as an option rather than a requirement — the premise the whole platform rests on.
Dataverse builds in role-based security, business logic, and platform integration — a traditional DB leaves all that to app code.
Tables hold records, columns are typed attributes, relationships link tables so data is stored once and connected.
Form: a single record's display/editing layout. View: a filtered, sorted list definition over a table.
The platform's Excel-like formula language — logic and calculation in canvas apps and Dataverse without code.
Describe the data you need in natural language; Copilot drafts tables, columns, and relationships for refinement.
The container for apps, flows, agents, and a Dataverse database, with its own security boundary — the dev/test/prod unit.
Environment roles govern who makes/uses; Dataverse security roles control table, row, and column access.
Solutions package work; Power Platform pipelines promote them dev → test → prod as governed, repeatable deployments.
Blank-screen freedom: drag controls, wire logic with Power Fx, connect to anything — task-focused and mobile-friendly.
Interface generated from Dataverse tables — consistent forms, views, dashboards for record-centric, process-heavy work.
Describe the business problem; AI plans the whole solution — tables, apps, automations — as one refinable design.
Full-code applications by professional developers, running inside Power Platform's governance and Dataverse foundation.
Describe the app in natural language → Copilot generates a working canvas or model-driven app → refine. The vibe experience keeps that loop conversational.
A canvas app is screens holding controls — labels, galleries, buttons, inputs. Each control has properties set with Power Fx expressions rather than event-handler code.
A control that repeats a layout once per record in a data source, which is how canvas apps show lists without a loop being written.
Granting other users access, which requires both permission on the app and permission on the data behind it — an app shared without data access opens but shows nothing.
A built-in review that flags formula errors, performance problems, and accessibility issues before an app is shared.
Cloud: connector-based automation between services. Desktop: RPA driving Windows apps that have no API.
One trigger starts a cloud flow (event, schedule, or manual); actions are the connector steps that follow, shaped by conditions and loops.
First-class routing of requests: approve/reject with comments recorded, flow continues on the outcome.
AI extracts structured data from invoices and forms; flows push it into business systems.
Describe the automation in natural language and Copilot drafts the flow — works for cloud flows and (by description or demonstration) desktop flows.
Approvals, Teams notifications, Outlook mail handling, SharePoint changes, Forms submissions, document automation.
An agent's authored conversation paths — trigger phrases recognise the request, the path resolves it; generative answers cover the gaps.
Websites, SharePoint, documents, Dataverse — grounding so the agent answers from real content.
What lets agents act: agent flows run processes mid-conversation; MCP servers connect external systems via a standard protocol.
Where a built agent is published: Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, websites, and more — one build, many surfaces.
The org-wide registry and control plane for agents: identities, governed access, security and compliance policy.
Sessions, resolution/escalation rates, topic traffic — usage and adoption analytics in Copilot Studio.
Scripted test conversations scored against the agent — the test suite that catches regressions before users do.
The example utterances that teach an agent when a topic applies. They are samples for matching, not an exhaustive list of accepted wording.
Letting an agent answer from its knowledge sources when no authored topic matches, instead of falling through to a dead end.
A conversational agent responds when someone talks to it; an autonomous agent is started by an event or schedule and acts without a person in the conversation.
Making a built agent available on its configured channels. Changes stay in the authoring canvas until published, so testing does not affect live users.
How an agent identifies the user so it can act on their behalf and respect their permissions, rather than reaching data everyone can see.
